correctness.rationale: The finite parameters and graph/valuation definitions are explicit. For k<=b cyclic placement yields floor/ceil values; a>=k and b>=k ensure enough zero connectors, and low-bundle storage leaves a removable valued vertex in every high bundle. For k>=a a matching of p=a+b-k edges avoids two ones when W<=k, or absorbs every zero in zero-one edges when W>k; all remaining singles and pairs differ in value by at most one and pairs permit outer deletion. For b<k<a all-one values force a singleton and a connected bundle with at least three vertices, violating outer-EF1. The actual bundled standard-library checker independently enumerated 3362 small profiles and ran 5451 construction profiles; these are tests rather than unrestricted proofs.

evidence: Bei et al. Proposition 4.8 guarantees ordinary EF1 for every number of agents no larger than either bipartition side, for arbitrary valuations. It does not impose outer deletion or characterize the high-agent segment.

value.rationale: An explicit complete connected-fair-division spectrum for an infinite, natural and often nontraceable bipartite graph class answers the sharply parameterized existence question prompted by recent spectrum research. The constructive matching and cyclic-balance regimes bridge a genuine gap between previous low-k and generic terminal positive guarantees, and the all-one obstruction matches the boundaries. It is a structural classification, not an arbitrary tiny parameter slice.
